last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Mon 08-31, day 20, Monday MORNING (08:34 IST) — a morning session, coffee-first, and the shape was the Deep-Dive I trailed last night. PAID THE TRAILER PROPERLY: the pull/push carve got its real payload — Tamil uses ONE verb for 'ask' and 'listen' (paattu kekkren / avan kitta ketten), because it files them under DIRECTION, not under mouth-vs-ear. Gave the noun halves too: 'sol' IS the word (oru sol), so sollu is literally 'to word'; 'kelvi' is the question, same root as kekku. Each direction has a noun welded to its verb. That reframes his three ear-misses as reasonable rather than stupid — English gives no reason to think ask and hear are relatives. ALSO PAID THE -kren DEBT the maami knock left open (cloud Anna promised it and fobbed him off): -ren/-kren = happening now and it's me, and kekk-uren is that sticker riding the very verb we were discussing. Kept pottu-kren (the self-benefactive) in my pocket as a hook. NO PRODUCTION DEMANDED on any of the lore — break contract honoured before any collect. MISSION UNFIRED, AND IT WAS MY FAULT: 'didn't find an opening.' The op needed the room to ask him a question with a NO inside it, and the room does not do that on schedule — it feeds him, asks what he did, tells him things. The 08-26 law (a mission must be an ANSWER) was obeyed; what I got wrong was the FREQUENCY of the trigger. Count how often the room actually speaks that opening, not just whether the slot is an answer. No guilt taken, none given. THE FIND OF THE MORNING — THE PERSON TAIL IS AN ECHO, NOT A CHOICE. Four fires: (1) 'athai kitta sonniyaa?' → 'innikki solra' — stem right, ORDER RIGHT, wrong person on the tail (-a points at him, not at me). (2) 'what are you cooking' → 'enna semaya' — he handed me the NOUN where the verb was owed. (3) 'enga pora?' → 'enge poren' — he took the -en I had JUST handed him and stuck it on HER, the exact inverse of slip (1), inside four minutes. (4) 'nee enga pora?' → 'shop-ku poren' COLD, unaided, with the English noun dropped in and the dative on it — clean, and it came immediately after I laid the minimal pair down (naan poren / nee pora, naan solren / nee solra). SO: whichever tail he heard LAST is the one his mouth grabs. This is `person-marker` (now 4x — 08-08 left the human unmarked, 08-14 marked himself when -nga pointed at her, and today BOTH directions inside one scene). Commissioned to the soak lane as matched pairs, person marker the only moving part — the recipe that converted ponom in one cycle. THE SECOND FIND, NEW TAG `noun-for-verb`: he owns Tamil NOUNS and his hand reaches for them so the verb never has to fire. 'enna samayal' is a REAL line and I seated it rather than marking it wrong (the proven drawer medicine) — but it is the same exit he took on 08-19, where it got logged as english-word-order and the noun dodge underneath went unnamed. This matters more than it looks: every tail we chase rides on a VERB, and last night's law was 'make the stem automatic and the tail comes free.' If he routes around verbs, no stem ever goes automatic. Watch for the noun exit on every production ask. english-word-order LANDED — tested and closed. Three novel scenes this morning, unaided every time: 'innikki solra', 'enna semaya', 'enge poren' — time/question-word up front, verb at the end, no English frame translated across. It was the 12-day uncommissioned slip the ticket kept nagging about; it healed without a dose and the evidence is production, not a recast. Named it to him out loud and it was the win of the session. KEKKU HELD BACK ON PURPOSE: I deep-dove the FAMILY as a gift (stem work, no demand) and kept kekku out of every production slot, so the kekkuren AMBUSH is still clean and still unannounced. Fire it later this week. STILL OPEN: wrong-verb-direction has its soak dose from 08-30 — test whether it landed, do not re-order it. The -ttu-kren self-benefactive is a promised hook, unpaid. TOMORROW OFFERED: Table Rehearsal — mask-work at speed with athai and mama, every line an answer, person tails under pressure; low-power twin is Ear Day on the kekku/sollu tape that shipped last night, no answering. TONIGHT'S MISSION (trigger the room actually speaks): someone WILL ask him where he is going or what he is doing — it happens every day in that house. Answer with the verb and -en on the end, and do not let the noun out of your mouth first.

soak_order.focus: THE PERSON TAIL, AND NOTHING ELSE MOVING. He used the nee-tail on himself and then the naan-tail on her inside four minutes: the ending is an echo of whatever he heard last, not a choice. Permute ONLY the person marker on two verbs he already owns, in matched frames, back to back: நான் போறேன் / நீ போற, நான் சொல்றேன் / நீ சொல்ற. Do NOT permute tense, do NOT permute the verb, do NOT bring in a third person — -en is me, -a is you, and the contrast is the whole payload. This is the minimal-pair recipe that converted போனோம் in one cycle. Every other lexical item from lexicon.json. Never name a rule.
